summary: Enterprise Role Intelligence P2 — Knowledge Capture → Proposed Memory Review queue + chat memory + workspace RAG for AI runtime, tested end-to-end on backend + web. Backend: 13/13 pytest pass (34s, several Claude calls) — POST /enterprise/roles/{id}/capture with pasted text returns 1-3 anonymized proposed memories (approval_status='proposed', source_type='Manual', no Raj/Priya/Amit leakage); with {chat_id} it captures from chat messages (source_type='TeamNest chat', source_id set); empty payload → 400; unknown role → 404; unknown chat → 404. GET /enterprise/memories/review returns memories + pending_count with role_name joined. POST /enterprise/memories/{mid}/decide correctly rejects (removes from proposed queue) or approves (approval_status='approved', appears in /enterprise/roles/{id}/memories, respects edited title override); invalid decision → 400, unknown mid → 404. Closed loop verified: after approving 'P2 approved: disputed vendor invoices', POST /enterprise/roles/{id}/ask returned grounded=True with [S#] citations and no personal names. REGRESSION: inline @ai in chat still posts an AI answer within 40s (context-injection did not block); AI employee sandbox POST /ai-builder/employees/{eid}/sandbox still returns a reply. Web UI: /enterprise Review tab shows badge with count (9), 'proposed-memory' cards with editable title/textarea and Approve/Reject buttons — approve with an edited title AND reject both remove the card from the queue and fire the correct toast ('Approved — now in role knowledge' / 'Rejected'). Person profile → Knowledge tab: 'Capture knowledge' button opens capture-modal (paste textarea OR chat dropdown), submit triggers POST and shows toast '2 item(s) proposed — review in the Review queue', modal closes, and the two new memories appear at the top of the Review queue anonymized ('Urgent client escalation war-room process', 'Automatic 10% credit for missed escalation SLA'). The earlier approved memories appear on Priya's Knowledge tab in the 'Approved role knowledge (source-grounded)' list. All flows working. One minor UX bug found: badge count on the Review tab is loaded once on EnterprisePage mount and is NOT decremented after Approve/Reject within the queue — stays at the stale value until page reload.

ui_bugs.issue: pendingReview state is fetched once in EnterprisePage useEffect() and never decremented when a memory is approved/rejected from the ReviewQueue child. The queue itself updates instantly (setItems filter), but the tab badge stays stale at its initial value until a full page reload. Recommend passing a decrement callback into <ReviewQueue/> or lifting pending_count into a shared store; alternatively re-GET /memories/review after every decide.

issues: The persistent 'AI Paralegal — Have you met' promo toast (bottom-right, fixed) partially overlaps the Capture-knowledge submission toasts. Not blocking, but the promo is stacked above the sonner toast and can visually crowd the confirmation message on smaller viewports.

action_items: Fix Review-tab badge staleness: decrement / re-fetch pending_count after every approve/reject decision so the [data-testid='review-badge'] number stays in sync with the queue.
(Optional) Consider dismissing / hiding the 'AI Paralegal — Have you met' promo toast while on the Capture flow so it doesn't visually crowd the propose-knowledge sonner confirmation.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/enterprise.py capture_knowledge() reads the entire chat history via build_chat_context(limit=30) but only truncates to 6000 chars downstream in propose_memories_from_text — for very large 30-msg chats this can silently drop older context. Consider trimming at build_chat_context or at least logging the truncation.

routes/enterprise.py review_queue() sorts by created_at DESC but the badge (pending_count) is computed with a separate count_documents call inside the same handler — an extra round trip. Could be derived from len(rows) when the page size is above pending, or cached with the query for smaller workspaces.

services/enterprise_intelligence.py propose_memories_from_text() falls back to a single naive 'Captured note' record whenever the LLM raises OR returns non-JSON. If the LLM returns an empty [] on purpose (nothing worth keeping), it does correctly return []; but the try/except also swallows LLM auth failures — a bad key would silently insert 'Captured note' junk. Suggest distinguishing 'model returned []' (empty is valid) from 'model call failed' (fallback with confidence 0.2 + a debug log).

services/enterprise_intelligence.py: anonymization is enforced ONLY by the system-prompt instruction ('never include any individual\'s personal name'). All 8 backend anonymization assertions passed today, but this is a soft guarantee — recommend adding a post-filter that redacts workspace employee_name matches before insert, same as noted for ask_previous_role in iteration_101.

services/ai_runtime.py build_chat_context() excludes message_type in ['ai_question','build_progress'] but does NOT exclude 'ai_answer' — the prior AI reply is INCLUDED in the next @ai prompt with the same 'AI:' role prefix. That's the intended chat memory, but if the previous AI answer was very long (>600 chars per line truncation OK, but 16 rows summed can be ~9600 chars) it may dominate the prompt. Consider a per-line char cap of 300 (not 600) or a total context cap of 4000 chars.

routes/enterprise.py capture_knowledge() checks chat access with 'member_ids: current[id]' but the chat lookup returns only {id: 1}; the projection is correct. However the audit log entry ('knowledge_captured') only records count + source_type and NOT the chat_id or role_id — makes audit-trail forensics harder. Add source_id + role_id to the audit meta.

EnterprisePage.jsx ReviewQueue L134: badge and queue are not sourced from the same fetch — the parent's `pendingReview` state can stale-drift (see UI bug). Also, the 'confidence %' rendering uses Math.round(m.confidence * 100) — if confidence is null it renders '0%'. Nudge to display 'unknown' when null.

EnterpriseProfile.jsx CaptureModal L237: the request payload always sends the chosen chat_id when the dropdown has a value, even if the user then typed something into the textarea. UX-wise, the textarea should be disabled (already hidden with !chatId) but the priority is fine. Consider showing a lock icon on the textarea when a chat is selected.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all core flows work; badge staleness minor)

Run: `cd /app/backend && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> python -m pytest tests/test_iteration103_p2_capture_review.py -v`. Web selectors verified: ent-tab-review, review-badge, review-queue, review-empty, review-{id}, review-title-{id}, review-content-{id}, review-approve-{id}, review-reject-{id}; person-{id} cards on the People tab; ptab-knowledge (kebab-cased), capture-knowledge-btn, capture-modal, capture-text, capture-chat, capture-submit. LLM occasionally returns 0 proposed items when the source text is thin — the capture test relaxes this to 1-3. Two prior curl test runs from other testing agents already stacked storage packs (from iter_102) and additional proposed memories, so the workspace is cumulative.
rca of the issue: Badge staleness: EnterprisePage useEffect() calls /memories/review once and stores pending_count in local state; the ReviewQueue child fetches memories independently and updates its own list with setItems on decide, but there is no upward signal to the parent to re-fetch. Fix: pass an onDecided() callback prop to ReviewQueue and re-GET /memories/review in the parent (cheap), OR move pendingReview state into a shared context / react-query cache keyed by the same URL.
